research_question: What is the global scale of seabird bycatch in trawl fisheries? How effective are mitigation measures in reducing this bycatch in the most affected species and regions?
objectives: To estimate a global total of seabird bycatch in trawl fisheries; To conduct a gap analysis; To identify the seabird families and species that are most susceptible to bycatch in trawl fisheries; To compare bycatch totals or fishery-wide bycatch rates before and after the introduction of mitigation measures
variables: Seabird bycatch rates; Bycatch totals; Fishing effort; Species affected; Geographical regions; Mitigation measures; Observer coverage; Data gaps and uncertainties; Cryptic mortality; Life-history characteristics of seabirds
analytical_methods: Literature Review; Data Extraction; Standardization of Bycatch Rates; Gap Analysis; Species Susceptibility Analysis; Assessment of Mitigation Measures
results: Global Seabird Bycatch Estimate: 44,000 seabirds per year; Variation in Bycatch Rates: Bycatch rates were found to be highly variable across different trawl fisheries; Geographical Distribution of Bycatch: Australia, New Zealand, South America, and southern Africa; Species Most Affected: Albatrosses, large petrels, and gannets; Effectiveness of Mitigation Measures: Offal management and Bird Scaring Lines have been effective; Data Gaps: European and Asian waters; Monitoring Challenges: Observer coverage 10% of fishing effort; Implications for Conservation: Seabird bycatch in trawl fisheries is one of the highest threats to seabird populations globally
limitations: Data Gaps and Incomplete Coverage; Variability in Bycatch Rates; Low Observer Coverage; Cryptic Mortality; Inconsistent Reporting and Monitoring Protocols; Limited Regional Focus; Dependence on Existing Literature
keywords: Albatrosses; Bycatch mitigation; Cryptic mortality; Fishing effort; Gannets; Global bycatch; Petrels; Seabird bycatch; Seabirds; Threatened species; Trawl fisheries
applicability_or_link: Bycatch Assessment; Identification of Critical Habitat Areas; Mitigation Measures; Data Gaps and Monitoring; Methodological Guidance; Mitigation Strategies; Extrapolation Frameworks; Global Context and Conservation Efforts
